content: Fluocinolone is a medication prescribed to alleviate symptoms such as itching, redness, dryness, crusting, scaling, inflammation, and discomfort associated with various skin conditions. It may also be used for other purposes as determined by your doctor. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Fluocinolone is available in different forms, including ointment, cream, solution, shampoo, and oil, with varying strengths for application on the skin. Typically, it is applied two to four times daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use fluocinolone exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it, or apply it more frequently than prescribed. Avoid applying it to other areas of your body or covering the treated area with a bandage or wrap unless instructed to do so by your doctor. Before applying the medication, wash or soak the affected area thoroughly unless doing so irritates your skin. Apply the ointment, cream, solution, or oil sparingly in a thin layer and gently rub it in. If using the shampoo, wet your hair and scalp, apply the shampoo, gently massage your scalp, and rinse with water. For scalp solutions, part your hair, apply a small amount of the medication to the affected area, and rub it in gently. Protect the area from washing or rubbing until the solution dries. You may wash your hair as usual but not immediately after applying the medication. Avoid prolonged use of fluocinolone on the face, genital and rectal areas, skin folds, or armpits unless directed by your doctor. If applying it to your face, ensure it does not come into contact with your eyes. When using fluocinolone on a child’s diaper area, avoid tight-fitting diapers or plastic pants, as these may increase side effects. Do not apply cosmetics or other skin preparations to the treated area without consulting your doctor. If your doctor instructs you to wrap or bandage the treated area, follow these steps: Wash or soak the area thoroughly. While the skin is still moist, gently rub the medication into the affected areas. Cover the area with plastic wrap (e.g., Saran Wrap or Handi-Wrap). Secure the plastic with gauze, an elastic bandage, or adhesive tape on normal skin adjacent to the treated area. Alternatively, use plastic gloves for hands, plastic bags for feet, or a shower cap for the scalp. Seal the edges of the plastic wrap carefully to ensure it adheres closely to the skin. If the area is moist, leave the edges partially unsealed or puncture the wrap to allow excess moisture to escape. Leave the plastic wrap in place for the duration specified by your doctor, typically no more than 12 hours per day. Cleanse the skin and reapply the medication each time a new plastic wrap is applied. Contact your doctor if the treated area worsens or if you experience burning, swelling, redness, or oozing of pus. Do not discontinue treatment abruptly without consulting your doctor. Before using fluocinolone, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to fluocinolone or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially cancer chemotherapy agents, other topical medications, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have an infection or a history of diabetes, glaucoma, cataracts, circulation disorders, or immune disorders. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using fluocinolone, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Fluocinolone may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: Drying or cracking of the skin Acne Itching Burning Changes in skin color If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: Severe skin rash Difficulty breathing or swallowing Wheezing Signs of a skin infection, such as redness, swelling, or oozing pus If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store fluocinolone in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat, and do not allow it to freeze. Dispose of any outdated or unused medication properly. Do not use it to treat other skin conditions. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, ask your pharmacist.
